one_line: A collaborative cloud-architecture canvas where agents edit, audit, price, and compile infrastructure designs.
what_it_does: Overhead presents a web-native architecture canvas with structured WebMCP actions for adding and connecting services, live state shared with humans and teammates, AWS price-source-backed cost calculation, self-auditing, and infrastructure-code compilation.
leverage_rationale: Structured verbs and shared document state make agent edits to an architecture canvas more precise and repeatable than coordinate-based UI driving, while the claimed pricing, auditing, and compilation workflow is meaningfully agent-centered. A general-purpose agent could likely approximate parts of the workflow, so the evidence does not establish transformative indispensability.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies structural WebMCP verbs such as add_service, connect, and patch_state rather than coordinate interaction.
Packet claims humans, teammates, and their agents share one document object in ephemeral rooms.
Packet claims agent-accessible pricing, auditing with citations, state patching, and compilation to infrastructure code.
Frame sheets visibly show a node-based architecture/workflow canvas, but tool invocation itself is not legible.
execution_rationale: The packet is coherent and shows a consistently rendered, interactive-looking node canvas with changing layouts, selection/configuration states, prompt controls, and supporting packaging. However, the frame sheets do not legibly demonstrate an end-to-end cost calculation, audit, compile, or deployment result, so execution is claimed rather than fully observed.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets consistently show the Overhead dark canvas, sidebar, connected colored nodes, input area, and changing workflow states.
Frames show apparent node insertion/selection and a configuration or inspector panel.
Devpost packaging aligns with the stated cloud-architecture canvas concept.
No legible success state, generated infrastructure artifact, cost output, or deployment result is visible in the frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Cloud architects, developers, and infrastructure teams have a concrete problem: architecture design, pricing, documentation, and deployable code are fragmented across tools. A shared canvas that keeps structure, sourced costs, audits, and compilation together could provide substantial value, though the packet only partially demonstrates the promised end-to-end outcome.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies friction from stale agent copies, disconnected component/cost/code tools, and documentation that is not kept aligned.
Packet claims real AWS SKU pricing with source URLs and compilation to CDK/CloudFormation and diagrams.
Frame sheets visibly show a workflow/architecture editing surface suitable for the stated audience.
The evidence does not visibly verify the accuracy of pricing or successful code generation.
creativity_rationale: The combination of live human-agent architecture editing, sourced infrastructure pricing, self-auditing, bidirectional diagram conversion, and code compilation is an ambitious and memorable synthesis for a hackathon. The visual node-canvas interaction is familiar, but the pursued combination and collaboration model are notably original.
creativity_evidence: Concept unifies architecture drawing, live agent collaboration, cost calculation, auditing, and infrastructure compilation in one document.
Packet claims diagrams can be converted back and forth into priced editable drawings.
The product framing of turning any agent into a cloud architect is clear and consistently presented.
Frame sheets show a populated, editable-looking graph rather than only a static promotional page.
usability_note: The canvas, sidebar, prompt area, and node configuration states suggest a usable workflow editor, but small/unreadable frame text and lack of a clearly shown completed result limit confidence about practical usability.
red_flags: Frame sheets are largely UI-presence and editing evidence; labels and outputs are too small to verify.
No video transcript is provided and the packet marks video=false despite supplied frame sheets.
Claims of real-time pricing, audits, compilation, and deployment are not visibly proven end-to-end.
standouts: Strong WebMCP-centered shared-state concept rather than a superficial action wrapper.
Ambitious integration of architecture editing, source-backed costs, auditing, and code generation.
Consistent product identity and coherent node-canvas presentation across frames and Devpost packaging.
advance_reason: Advance: the project presents a clear, ambitious WebMCP-native developer workflow with credible visible UI evidence and a strong problem/solution fit. Keep execution and leverage below the top band because the packet does not visibly prove agent tool invocation or a completed end-to-end output.
